SMTO-LLM-0023 — The model service couldn't find the address SMTO used

GUID: 1975e1fa-9668-447f-aa67-34ddb1036e2a
Slug: provider-endpoint-unavailable
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO reached the model service, but the address in SMTO's settings doesn't lead to a model there. This doesn't mean the whole service is down.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and compare Endpoint with the address your provider gives. Many end in /v1, like the default http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1. SMTO adds the rest of the address itself, so a missing or extra part leads nowhere.
  2. Make sure Model names a model this service offers; select Discover models to see the list. A model name the service doesn't know can also lead to an address that doesn't exist.
  3. Select Save Main, then Check saved model. When it passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). The test proves the corrected address works, and the failed request did nothing that needs undoing.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model service; they can confirm the correct address and model name. Don't delete SMTO's data or other settings to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider returned HTTP 404 for the requested endpoint or model route (provider_endpoint_unavailable), pointing to a wrong base path or unavailable route rather than a full service outage.

What this means

  • The provider returned HTTP 404 for the requested route. A wrong base path, unavailable model route or intentionally hidden resource can produce this response. It does not establish that the whole service is down.

Why this can happen

  • The requested endpoint or model route was not found or was not disclosed to this client.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the configured base URL and model identifier with the routes the provider serves. Confirm both with the operator instead of adding guessed path segments.

How to fix it

  • SMTO calls the role's Endpoint plus /chat/completions and /models. Verify the base URL includes the provider's API prefix (often /v1) and that the model route exists, for example by requesting the endpoint's /models directly. Correct the Endpoint or model in Settings › Setup › Model routing, test with Check saved model, then resume.
  • Verify the provider’s supported base URL and model route in Model Configuration, then test the corrected route.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open LLM Endpoint: model-configuration / llm_base_url. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended route returns a model response instead of HTTP 404.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Status classification describes this model request and grants no authority to replay earlier tools.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
